sections.h2: What are my main options for selling a house in Lauderdale Lakes?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: an agent listing, a sale handled by you alone, or a direct purchase by an investor. Each trades speed against price and effort, so weigh the house's problems and your calendar first.

Broward County offices (property appraiser, tax collector, clerk of the circuit court) handle the records behind any sale here, while the city site covers local services. In late 2026 the city was promoting a pitch competition for graduates of its Business Growth Initiative, a sign of how it is courting small businesses.

  • Listings reward a clean, updated unit and patience through showings.
  • Going alone keeps the agent's share but hands you every contract and disclosure.
  • An investor purchase fits deferred repairs, occupied units, liens or a fixed deadline.

sections.h2: What is Lauderdale Lakes like, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Lauderdale Lakes is a compact city of about four square miles in the middle of Broward County, centered on the crossroads of State Road 7 (US 441) and Oakland Park Boulevard. The city incorporated on June 22, 1961, when roughly 300 people lived in what was then a rural area of farms and grazing land.

State Road 7 was a two-lane undivided road at the time, and the first city hall sat in a construction trailer. Growth through the 1960s and 1970s filled the area with neighborhoods around the lakes that give the city its name. Voters moved to a Mayor, City Commission and City Manager structure in March 1998, and the city's own history page describes goals of reviving its commercial corridor, upgrading infrastructure, adding parks and raising property values.

Police service comes through the Broward Sheriff's Office, with 107 of its personnel serving the city according to the history page. A seller can lean on that central location, because commuters and investors both look at that crossroads first.

  • Share the street and cross streets in the listing so buyers can place the house.
  • Note any lake or canal frontage on the survey.
  • Tell buyers whether the home sits near the State Road 7 corridor.

sections.h2: Can I sell Lauderdale Lakes property that a tenant occupies?
sections.html:
Yes, but the lease keeps running after a sale contract is signed. A buyer either takes the unit with the tenant in it or waits for the landlord to end the tenancy through the statutory notice steps in Chapter 83.

Notice lengths depend on the problem. Missed rent draws a 3-day demand (weekends and court holidays do not count), and a lease violation the tenant can fix draws 7 days to cure. Periodic tenancies end on 30 days' notice for month-to-month arrangements and 60 days for year-to-year ones. A lease cannot waive these rules, and delivery can be by mail, hand, e-mail or a copy left at the unit.

  • Ask each buyer in writing whether they accept the lease as is.
  • Pass the rent roll and deposit amount to the closing agent.
  • Keep a copy of each notice and proof of how it was delivered.

sections.h2: How do Broward property taxes affect my closing?
sections.html:
Value is fixed on January 1, bills follow in November, and your months of ownership are settled at closing. The Broward County Property Appraiser handles values and exemptions and lists 954-357-6830 for questions.

Property tax dates printed by the Florida Department of Revenue
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Deadline to file for exemptions
AugustNotice of Proposed Property Taxes mailed
25 days after the noticePetition window for a value challenge
NovemberTax bills mailed
April 1Unpaid taxes turn delinquent

Paying early earns a discount that shrinks from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February. A buyer's first bill can run higher than yours because a sale returns the house to full assessed value (s. 193.155).

sections.h2: What if my Lauderdale Lakes house is vacant or in poor repair?
sections.html:
A vacant or worn house still sells, but the buyer pool changes, and an empty building draws extra attention from insurers, neighbors and code staff. Lenders balk at deferred repairs, while an investor prices the work and closes without an inspection fight.

A homestead exemption ends once the home is rented or stops being your permanent residence. If you moved out and the exemption still sits on your parcel, tell the property appraiser instead of letting the roll carry it.

  • Walk the property and list defects before you accept any offer.
  • Check the Broward tax collector for unpaid balances.
  • Ask the title company about liens that could delay closing.

sections.h2: What if I am behind on the mortgage?
sections.html:
Florida foreclosures run through the courts, so you usually have time to sell before a judgment sale. After judgment, the clerk sets the auction between 20 and 35 days out unless the lender agrees to longer (s. 45.031).

Talk to your servicer and the closing agent about a payoff statement, and ask whether a short sale or an investor purchase fits your balance.

Open every letter from the lender and the court, and write the response date on a calendar. Silence is the costliest choice, because deadlines keep running whether or not you answer. A neutral third party, such as a housing counselor or a legal aid office, can read the papers with you before you decide anything.

sections.h2: How should I prepare a Lauderdale Lakes house before showing it?
sections.html:
Start with the things buyers notice from the curb: the roof line, the yard, the front door and any peeling paint. On an older house, buyers often ask about the age of the roof, the electrical panel, the plumbing and the air handler. A one-page list of what was replaced and when answers those questions before they become negotiating points.

Clear out clutter and walk each room with a notepad. Note stains, soft floors, door-frame cracks and anything that smells of damp. Florida humidity punishes closed-up houses, so run the air conditioning and open the blinds before every showing.

sections.h2: How do I compare a listing with an investor offer?
sections.html:
Write each path as a net figure. For a listing, take the expected sale price, subtract the agent's commission, the repairs a buyer's inspector will demand, carrying costs for each month on the market, and closing costs. For an investor offer, subtract only what the contract assigns to you.

Then compare timing. A listing may take months and can fall through at financing or appraisal. An investor sale can close within a few weeks, but the price is lower. Ask any buyer to put the closing date, deposit, repair responsibility and fee split in writing, and read every line before signing.

  • Price, deposit and whether it is refundable.
  • Closing date and who picks the title company.
  • Who pays for repairs found in inspection.
  • What happens to any security deposit held for a tenant.

faqs.q: How far apart are the city's roads and where is the center?
faqs.a: The city is about four square miles, centered on State Road 7 (US 441) at Oakland Park Boulevard, according to its history page.

faqs.q: Can I sell while a tenant lives in the house?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease stays in force, so the buyer takes the house with the tenant or waits for a lawful notice process to end the tenancy (s. 83.56, s. 83.57). Whichever route you pick, put it in the sales contract so the title company and the tenant both know the plan.

faqs.q: Will the buyer inherit my capped assessment?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the property returns to just value the following January 1 (s. 193.155).

faqs.q: When do Broward tax bills go out?
faqs.a: In November. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1, so ask the Broward tax collector for an exact balance before closing.
The city's history page says Broward Sheriff's Office personnel, 107 of them, serve alongside city staff.
